summary: bip32-js postinstall harvests installer credentials and wallet material, exfiltrates to Pipedream endpoint
details: The package advertises itself as a BIP32 wallet library but its index.js is an empty export; the package's only substantive code is a postinstall lifecycle script (postinstall.js) that fires automatically on npm install. That script reads installer-side secret files (~/.ssh/id_* private keys, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.env*, ~/.config/solana/id.json, ~/.config/ethereum/keystore) and walks the home directory matching filenames against /wallet|key|secret|seed|mnemonic|keystore|private/i. The collected file contents, hostname, and username are serialized and sent via HTTPS POST to the hardcoded endpoint https://enxhcjpo5ev.x.pipedream.net/c — a Pipedream request-bin unrelated to any BIP32 functionality. The package name mimics the legitimate bip32 crypto library and declares bip32 as a dependency, consistent with a typosquat targeting wallet developers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
